rows.narration: Most small rooms are not actually short of space. They are short of sightlines, light and vertical thinking, and all three are things you can fix this weekend.

rows.narration: In this video we are going through 5 of them, one at a time, with the reasoning behind each one and exactly how to apply it in a real home.
That takes us to number 1. Hang your curtains close to the ceiling, not to the window frame.
rows.query: floor to ceiling curtains living room

rows.narration: The eye reads the top of the curtain rod as the top of the wall, so mounting the rod high stretches the whole room upward and makes a standard eight-foot ceiling feel far taller than it is.
Mount the rod four to six inches below the ceiling line and let the panels break just barely on the floor.
Buy the longest ready-made length you can find, usually ninety-six or one hundred and eight inches, and widen the rod so the panels stack off the glass.
Number 2 on the list. Why does this keep coming up in well-designed homes? Add one oversized plant instead of five small ones.
A cluster of small pots reads as clutter and needs constant attention. One large plant reads as architecture and softens the hard corners of a room.
A fiddle leaf fig, a bird of paradise, or an olive tree in a floor basket fills vertical space beautifully.
Put it where two walls meet, and if your light is poor, a good-quality faux tree is a completely legitimate choice.
Make the window treatments oversized. Panels roughly twice the width of the window so they still look full when closed, hung high and wide, and hemmed to just kiss the floor.
Generous fabric is one of the clearest signals of money in a room, because skimpy curtains are the default in every rental.
It is a small change that changes the whole read of the room.
Idea number 4. Leave the corners of the room resolved. Empty, awkward corners are where a room visibly runs out of ideas, and stuffing them with random small objects makes it worse.
rows.query: corner plant floor lamp living room

rows.narration: A tall plant, a floor lamp, a leaning mirror or a single chair with a small table. One considered object beats three leftovers.
Do that much and the rest of the room starts to make more sense.
Now for something you can do in an afternoon. Number 5, and this one is a favorite. Be careful with this one, because it is easy to get backwards. Do not block the window.
Daylight is the most valuable thing in a room, and a tall piece of furniture in front of the glass costs you light in every direction.
Keep anything above windowsill height away from the window wall. If a piece must go there, choose something low or open in construction.
That is all 5 of them. If you have a room you are stuck with, leave it in the comments and it might end up in a future video.
